messages.author: bd837dec56edd1af
messages.subject: introductions
parts:
Hey everyone, join up and say hello! Everyone is welcome to join, whether you are an experienced R user, a new user or just curious. I'm hoping to organize some informal (i.e. pub-based) meetups over the summer, and to start formal monthly meetups with presentations in the autumn. Please post a short intro of yourself when you join so we can get the conversation started.

I am a software developer trained as an economist, and I've been using R for about 10 years. I use R regularly and do a lot of work with documenting R and writing refreshable documents which incorporate R output, via an open source software package I wrote called Dexy (http://dexy.it).

messages.author: 703158e211c97e0e
messages.subject: Introducing myself
parts:
Hi folks,

my name is Dietmar Janetzko. I am working as a lecturer at the School
of Computing
at the National College of Ireland in Dublin.

There are computer systems that lock you into one particular
intellectual level and others that help
you to go beyond that level - well ... if you are ready to overcome
some obstacles sometimes. R is definitively a
system of the latter kind. I use R for many years and I am struck by
the breadth of the various types
of analysis that are being developed under the R flag and which are
made available to the general audience.

My own work is related to data mining, statistics, social network
analysis and other data analysis areas
and I am looking forward to exchange R-related things with other like-
minded people.



Best



Dietmar

I'm a statistician/lecturer working in the areas of biochemistry,
